headline: Boeing posts larger loss than expected as Air Force One costs rise
summary: STORY: Shares of Boeing rose as much as five percent Tuesday morning after releasing quarterly results that showed its turnaround plans are gaining momentum.It posted a larger-than-expected quarterly loss but generated positive free cash flow, which it attributed in part to higher customer payments than anticipated.Much of the loss came from a $280 million charge due to higher engineering costs to ensure it delivers two delayed Air Force One plane replacements in 2028. Boeing signed a $3.9 billion fixed-price contract in 2018 for the 747 jets that is now four years behind schedule and more than $1 billion over budget.On a per-share basis, the quarterly loss was wider than expected but smaller than the same quarter a year earlier.The U.S. planemaker is maintaining its guidance of $1 billion to $3 billion in free cash flow for the year, which would be its first positive result since 2023, as it increases production of its best-selling 737 MAX narrow-body jets.
